findings.title: Restore tenant verification before approving invoices
findings.explanation: The changed predicate authorizes any session with the `billing-approver` role without comparing `session.tenantId` to `invoice.tenantId`. Consequently, an approver authenticated for tenant A can be authorized to approve an invoice belonging to tenant B. Restore the tenant equality check alongside the role check, with a regression test covering a cross-tenant approver denial.
findings.failurePath: A tenant-A session with `roles` containing `billing-approver` and a tenant-B invoice reaches `canApproveInvoice`; the new expression returns true solely from the role membership, allowing the approval path to proceed across the tenant boundary.

candidates.invariant: Invoice approval must require both the billing-approver role and a session tenant matching the invoice tenant.
candidates.counterexample: A billing approver from tenant A can approve tenant B's invoice because the predicate now ignores invoice.tenantId.
candidates.evidenceNeeded: Confirm approval entry points rely on canApproveInvoice and verify the authorization contract or tests require cross-tenant approval to be rejected.

findings.title: Restore tenant verification before approving invoices
findings.explanation: The changed predicate authorizes any session with the `billing-approver` role without comparing `session.tenantId` to `invoice.tenantId`. Consequently, an approver authenticated for tenant A can be authorized to approve an invoice belonging to tenant B. Restore the tenant equality check alongside the role check, with a regression test covering a cross-tenant approver denial.
findings.failurePath: A tenant-A session with `roles` containing `billing-approver` and a tenant-B invoice reaches `canApproveInvoice`; the new expression returns true solely from the role membership, allowing the approval path to proceed across the tenant boundary.
